step1_figure.description: The circuit is a series-shunt feedback amplifier where the input signal is applied to the gate of M1 and the feedback voltage is fed back to the source via a resistive voltage divider (R1 and R2) connected to the output node. This topology samples output voltage (shunt sampling) and mixes voltage at the input (series mixing), stabilizing the voltage gain at approximately 1 + R2/R1.

closed_loop_gain.description: Closed-loop voltage gain ACL = v2/vs = AOL / (1 + AOL * beta)

source.reference: Equation for ACL on page 1119, between Eqs. (31.40) and (31.41)

equation.formula: ACL = AOL / (1 + AOL * beta) ≈ 1 / beta = 1 + R2 / R1
equation.explanation: Closed-loop voltage gain of the series-shunt amplifier determined by open-loop gain AOL and feedback factor beta = R1 / (R1 + R2). For large loop gain, ACL approaches 1 / beta.
equation.assumptions: AOL * beta >> 1, negligible reverse transmission through basic amplifier

sky130_expected.calculation: With R1 = 1 kΩ and R2 = 9 kΩ, beta = 1k / (1k + 9k) = 0.1 V/V. For typical AOL ≈ 100 V/V (40 dB), ACL = 100 / (1 + 100 * 0.1) = 100 / 11 = 9.09 V/V (19.17 dB). Ideally, ACL ≈ 1 / beta = 10 V/V (20 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Finite open-loop gain AOL (80 to 150 V/V) results in a closed-loop gain slightly below the ideal 1/beta = 10 V/V.

feedback_factor.description: Feedback factor beta representing the fraction of output voltage fed back to the input

equation.explanation: Voltage divider ratio set by feedback resistors R1 and R2 connected across the output.
equation.assumptions: Loading from the gate of M1 is negligible (MOSFET gate has infinite DC resistance)

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined purely by passive resistors R1 = 1 kΩ and R2 = 9 kΩ.

open_loop_gain.description: Open-loop voltage gain AOL including loading of feedback network

equation.explanation: Gain of the two cascaded gain stages including the loading of R1 and R2 in open-loop conditions.
equation.assumptions: Small-signal linearized model with ro effects simplified

sky130_expected.calculation: Stage 1 (PMOS input xm1 with degenerated source R1||R2 ≈ 900 Ω, loaded by active current source r_o ~ 50 kΩ): gm1 ≈ 0.5 mS -> Av1 ≈ -gm1*ro / (1 + gm1*(R1||R2)) ≈ -0.5m*50k / (1 + 0.45) ≈ -17.2 V/V. Stage 2 (NMOS common source xm2 + PMOS source follower buffer): Av2 ≈ -gm2*(ro || RL) ≈ -6 to -8 V/V. Overall AOL = Av1 * Av2 ≈ 100 to 120 V/V (~40 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical two-stage CMOS amplifier in SKY130 with source degeneration and active loads produces an open-loop gain between 34 dB and 46 dB.

source.reference: Text discussion of AOL * beta, page 1119

equation.explanation: The product of open-loop gain and feedback factor determining feedback desensitivity and bandwidth extension.

sky130_expected.reasoning: With AOL ≈ 110 V/V and beta = 0.1 V/V, loop gain T is approximately 11 (20.8 dB).

closed_loop_bandwidth.description: -3 dB cutoff frequency of the closed-loop voltage amplifier

equation.explanation: Negative feedback extends the open-loop -3dB bandwidth by the factor (1 + AOL * beta).
equation.assumptions: Dominant pole compensation by load capacitor Cload = 10 pF at output

sky130_expected.calculation: Output pole with Cload = 10 pF and closed-loop output resistance Rof ≈ 150 Ω: f_-3dB ≈ 1 / (2 * pi * Rof * Cload) = 1 / (2 * pi * 150 * 10e-12) ≈ 106 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: With a 10 pF load and source follower output buffer, closed-loop bandwidth is typically between 20 MHz and 200 MHz.

equation.explanation: Shunt sampling at the output reduces open-loop output impedance Ro by the feedback amount (1 + AOL * beta).
equation.assumptions: Basic amplifier output resistance Ro loaded by (R1 + R2)

sky130_expected.calculation: Open-loop output impedance of PMOS source follower xmsf is Ro ≈ 1 / gm_sf ≈ 1 / (1 mS) = 1000 Ω. With (1 + AOL * beta) ≈ 1 + 11 = 12: Rof = 1000 / 12 ≈ 83 Ω.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Shunt voltage feedback significantly reduces output resistance from the open-loop source follower level.

power_dissipation.description: Total quiescent DC power dissipation of the amplifier and bias circuit

source.reference: General circuit DC power consideration under VDD=1.8V

equation.explanation: Product of supply voltage VDD (1.8 V) and total DC current drawn from supply.
equation.assumptions: Circuit operating at nominal DC quiescent operating point

sky130_expected.calculation: Bias block draws ~100 µA, amplifier stages draw ~150 µA. Total current ≈ 250 µA. P_DC = 1.8 V * 250 µA ≈ 450 µW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Quiescent currents through reference bias generator and active gain branches sum to ~100 µA - 500 µA.

step3_testbench.description: Ngspice testbench measuring closed-loop gain (ACL), feedback factor (beta), -3dB bandwidth, and quiescent DC power dissipation for the series-shunt feedback amplifier.
